title: Mint Green Block Print Kurta Set: Style Guide for Women
excerpt: How to style a mint green hand block print kurta set for the office, brunch, puja, baby showers and travel, plus winter layering and care tips.
body:
A mint green hand block print kurta set is one of the easiest outfits to style: wear it with studs and loafers for the office, with pearls for brunch or a baby shower, and with gold jhumkas and the dupatta on both shoulders for a puja or haldi. Mint is fresh and light, and breathable block print cotton keeps you comfortable all day, whether you are in a heated office or a sunny garden.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. This set is hand block printed by karigars and stitched in our own Jaipur unit.*

**Quick answer**

- Office: small studs, a watch, the dupatta folded or skipped, loafers
- Brunch or baby shower: pearls, soft pink lip, the dupatta around the neck
- Puja or haldi: gold jhumkas, bindi, the dupatta on both shoulders
- Travel: a denim jacket or long cardigan, trainers or juttis
- Winter: a long camel coat, thermal leggings and boots

## Why choose mint green block print?

Mint is a soft, cool green that feels calm and fresh. It flatters most skin tones and looks especially lovely in daylight. It also pairs easily with gold, silver, pearls and oxidised jewellery.

Hand block printing gives the fabric character. Each print is stamped by hand with carved wooden blocks, so there are tiny, natural variations that make every piece unique. The [mint green hand block print cotton kurta set with hand work yoke](/products/mint-green-hand-block-print-cotton-kurta-pant-dupatta-set-with-hand-work-yoke/) adds a hand-worked yoke for a little extra detail near the face.

To understand the craft, read [hand block print vs screen print](/blog/hand-block-print-vs-screen-print-how-to-tell-the-difference/), which explains how to tell real hand block printing apart.

## How do I style it for each occasion?

| Occasion | Jewellery | Dupatta | Shoes | Extra |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Office | Studs, a watch | Folded on one shoulder or skipped | Loafers, block heels | Tailored blazer |
| Brunch | Pearl drops | Loosely around the neck | Ballet flats | Tote bag |
| Baby shower | Pearls, thin bangles | Over both shoulders | Juttis | Soft pink lip |
| Puja or haldi | Gold jhumkas, bindi | Over head or shoulders | Slip-ons | Flowers in a braid |
| Travel | Small hoops | In your bag | Trainers | Denim jacket |

## How do I wear it to the office?

Mint green is gentle enough for the office and still feels a little special. Skip the dupatta or fold it neatly over one shoulder. Add small gold studs, a watch and loafers or block heels. On a cold day, a tailored navy or camel blazer looks smart on top.

## How do I wear it to brunch or a baby shower?

For brunch, wear the dupatta loosely around your neck like a scarf. Add pearl drops and a soft pink or coral lip. Ballet flats keep it relaxed.

For a baby shower or godh bharai, drape the dupatta over both shoulders and add thin bangles. Mint is a lovely, gentle colour for these happy daytime events and looks fresh in photos.

## How do I wear it to a puja or haldi?

For a puja, drape the dupatta over your head or shoulders and keep jewellery simple. For a haldi, go a little more festive with gold jhumkas, a bindi and flowers in your hair. Block print cotton is easy to sit in on the floor and breathes well in a crowded room.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** Our karigars print each colour separately, lining up the wooden block by eye before pressing it onto the cotton. That is why the print feels soft and slightly uneven when you touch it. The cotton also gets softer with every wash, so a block print set becomes more comfortable the more you wear it.

## How do I wear it in winter?

Mint green is a summer colour, but it works in winter with the right layers. Wear thin thermal leggings under the pants and a fitted thermal top under the kurta. On top, a long camel, grey or cream coat looks lovely with mint. A soft grey shawl adds warmth indoors. Switch to boots outside and juttis indoors.

## How do I care for a block print kurta set?

Block print cotton is easy to care for, but a little attention keeps the colours fresh. Wash it separately in cold water with a mild detergent for the first few washes, as a little extra dye may release. Dry it in the shade, and iron on the reverse. Our full guide on [how to wash and care for block printed cotton](/blog/how-to-wash-and-care-for-block-printed-cotton-kurtis/) has step-by-step tips.

## Frequently asked questions

**What jewellery goes with a mint green kurta set?**
Gold, pearls, silver and oxidised jewellery all work. Gold feels festive, pearls feel soft, and oxidised silver feels boho.

**Can I wear mint green in winter?**
Yes. Layer with thermals underneath and a long camel, grey or cream coat on top.

**Does hand block print fade?**
Hand block print cotton can soften slightly over time. Wash in cold water, dry in the shade and avoid harsh detergents to keep colours fresh.

**Is mint green good for a baby shower?**
Yes. Mint is soft, fresh and joyful, which suits a baby shower or godh bharai beautifully.
